_README: SHORT FIELD LANDING DISTANCE, Cessna 182T NAV III, POH Section 5
Performance. Transcribed from the printed table supplied by the author.
DATA ONLY - NOTHING READS THIS YET. Consumer is roadmap item 5 Phase D
(performance), which is not built and not approved.
ONE WEIGHT, AND IT IS THE MAXIMUM LANDING MASS. The POH publishes this
table at 2950 lb only - it is NOT a weight axis with one row, and it must
never be interpolated or scaled by weight. A lighter aeroplane lands
SHORTER, so reading the 2950 lb figure for any legal landing weight errs
long, which is the safe direction and is presumably why one table suffices.
Stating that reasoning matters: the takeoff tables DO carry three weights,
so a shared interpolator that assumed a weight axis here would silently
invent one.
THE GRASS CORRECTION IS NOT THE TAKEOFF ONE. Landing adds 45% of the
ground roll; takeoff adds 15%. Two different numbers under near-identical
wording is exactly the shape this project keeps getting caught by, so the
corrections live with their own table and are never shared.
WHY IT CAN BE TRUSTED: the OFP workbook's Performance!F:H independently
carries 30 of these cells (PA 0-5000 x 5 temperatures), transcribed by the
author from the same POH. All 30 agree exactly, which is what makes the
PA 6000/7000/8000 rows - present here and absent from the workbook -
trustworthy read by the same method. test.js asserts that agreement.
AND THE TITLE CORROBORATES MLW A THIRD TIME: 2950 lb is what
Performance!W1:X3 draws as the MLW line and what the author stated, and it
is what this page is published at.

source.figure: SHORT FIELD LANDING DISTANCE AT 2950 POUNDS
source.suppliedBy: the flight school, as a printed-page image

conditions: Short field technique as specified in Section 4

corrections.headwind: Decrease distances 10% for each 9 knots headwind.
corrections.tailwind: For operation with tail winds up to 10 knots, increase distances by 10% for each 2 knots.
corrections.grassRunway: For operation on dry grass runway, increase distances by 45% of the GROUND ROLL figure.
corrections.flapsUp: If landing with flaps up, increase the approach speed by 10 KIAS and allow for 40% longer distances.

units: feet; each cell is [ground roll, total to clear a 50 ft obstacle]
